summary: Bhikkhu Pāsādika is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned an MA at Magadh University and a PhD at Punjabi University. He held posts at Punjabi University, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and the University of Marburg.
Bhikshuni Longlian was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Fazun in 1939 and Nenghai Shi.

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from around 1951 to 1975.

Bidia Dandaron was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov and Andrei Vostrikov, attending Saint Petersburg State University. In 1957, he served as a research fellow at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.

Bihani Sarkar works in Indology and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Hamburg and is attested as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University in 2026.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta, Sanskrit College and University, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later holding professorships at the University of Toronto and the University of Oxford.

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at Patna University and earned his PhD under Lionel David Barnett at SOAS University of London, later serving as department head at Patna University and Hon. Jt. Director at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.
Bing Chen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He became a professor at Sichuan University around 1987 and was attested as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.
Bingtao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University in 2008 and completed his PhD under Xue Yu at The Chinese University of Hong Kong by 2015.

Birgit Kellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura, later holding positions at the University of Vienna, Heidelberg University, and as director of the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu was an Indologist and historian who studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. From around 1916 to 1950, he headed the Sardar Government Museum and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and served at Sumer Public Library.
Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. As of 2026, he is a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das.

Biswanath Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society from around 1999 to 2001.
Bo Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander between 1958 and 1973, later holding a post there from around 1987 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a professorship at Dongguk University, attested between 2004 and 2015.
Bokar Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Kalu Rinpoche from around 1959 to 1989. He held a post at Bokar Monastery from around 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and earned a PhD from Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD under George C. Kerner at Michigan State University. He held posts at Florida International University, where he was attested as professor of philosophy in 2012.

Boris Turayev was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University from 1887 to 1891. He held a post at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1898 to 1920.
